question: Why does Arjuna call Krishna father and teacher?
premises: Krishna is father of moving and still beings
Krishna is venerable teacher of the universe
No equal or superior exists in three worlds
inference: Arjuna grounds his plea in Krishna's unmatched paternal and teaching authority
uncertainties: fused tvatsamo'styabhyadhikaḥ may be read as copula plus adjective
plain_english: You are father of the moving and still world, venerable teacher of this universe; none is equal to you, much less superior, in the three worlds of unmatched splendor.
